subject: Geopolitics
title: The Cuban Missile Crisis Intel
description: A fast breakdown of The Cuban Missile Crisis Intel for builders.

hook.text: A U-2 spy plane photographed Soviet missiles in Cuba. Kennedy had days to respond before they became operational.

buildup.text: Aerial reconnaissance — IMINT — detected the missile sites.

discovery.text: Intelligence gave Kennedy options. He chose a naval blockade instead of a strike because he had time and data.

twist.text: Soviet submarine captains nearly launched nuclear torpedoes during the crisis. One officer, Vasili Arkhipov, said no.

climax.text: The crisis demonstrated that intelligence is most valuable when it provides time for leaders to think, not just react.

punchline.text: One photograph and one officer saved the world.

quiz.question: How did intelligence shape Kennedy's response to the Cuban Missile Crisis?
options: It showed Cuba had no real military capability
Aerial photos gave him time and options to choose a blockade
Human spies in Moscow reported the Soviets would back down
